description: Extra names a fully-mapped venue is known by in the NHS ODS register, used by scripts/nhs/build-sites.mjs to recognise that a directory site is already covered, and by scripts/nhs/approve-plans.mjs to refuse a discovered map of a hospital that already ships as a venue. Most venues need no entry — their own name matches the ODS one closely enough. These are the ones where it doesn't: a venue called 'GOSH Wayfinder' shares no words with ODS's 'Great Ormond Street Hospital For Children', so without an alias it would get a duplicate, unnavigable pin sitting on top of the mapped venue. Add an entry whenever a mapped venue's display name diverges from its official name, or when one venue covers several ODS sites.
scoping: An alias is either a plain string, or {name, trustCode} when the name alone identifies more than one hospital. 'Queen Mary's Hospital' is St George's in Roehampton (mapped) and Oxleas' in Sidcup (not); a bare alias would hide Sidcup's map, so that one is scoped to RJ7. Use a plain string when the name is nationally unambiguous, and scope it when it isn't. A name that comes down to a single distinctive word after the common ones are dropped ('Wythenshawe', 'Lewisham', and 'London' from 'The Royal London Hospital') is ONLY used when scoped — one word matches far too much on its own, and unscoped it refused Evelina London's map for looking like the Royal London's.
